data.description: Investigate whether RiotPlan's MCP architecture can be simplified to eliminate the dual registration system for tools, resources, and prompts. Currently, adding a new MCP tool requires registration in two separate places (src/mcp/tools/index.ts and src/mcp/server.ts via registerTool()), which is error-prone and has already caused bugs during development.

data.content: From the plan-retrospectives-learning-loop Step 6 reflection: "This step took longer than expected because I initially forgot that RiotPlan uses a dual registration system for MCP tools. I implemented the tools in src/mcp/tools/ and registered them in the tools index, but completely missed that src/mcp/server.ts has its own manual tool registration with registerTool() calls. This caused the tools to be 'missing' from the MCP server even though they were properly implemented. The key learning: RiotPlan's MCP architecture has two registration points - one for internal use (src/mcp/tools/index.ts) and one for the MCP server itself (src/mcp/server.ts). Both must be updated when adding new tools."

data.note: Key finding: Resources and prompts do NOT have the dual registration problem. They use a single-loop registration pattern in server.ts. Only tools suffer from dual registration. The root cause is a schema format mismatch - tool files use JSON Schema, but server.ts registerTool() expects Zod schemas.

There's a count discrepancy: 35 tools in tools/index.ts but only 30 registerTool() calls in server.ts. This means 5 tools are defined but not registered with the MCP server - exactly the kind of silent failure this dual registration causes.

data.question: Can we unify on Zod schemas everywhere (tool files export Zod, server.ts consumes Zod directly) to eliminate the need for manual re-registration?
Could we adopt the same loop-based registration pattern that resources and prompts already use successfully?
What are the 5 tools that exist in tools/index.ts but are missing from server.ts registerTool() calls? Are these actual bugs?

data.name: Zod Schema Export + Auto-Registration Loop
data.description: Each tool file exports a Zod schema alongside the existing McpTool definition. The McpTool type gets a new optional field (e.g., `zodSchema: z.ZodRawShape`). server.ts replaces all 31 manual registerTool() calls with a single loop: `for (const tool of tools) { registerTool(tool.name, tool.description, tool.zodSchema); }`. The registerTool() helper function stays as-is (it handles context setup, error handling, heartbeats). JSON Schema inputSchema fields are removed or derived from Zod. Minimal refactor - mostly additive changes to tool files, then delete the manual calls from server.ts.
tradeoffs: Pro: Smallest diff - add zodSchema to each tool, delete manual calls from server.ts
Pro: registerTool() helper with its context/error/heartbeat logic stays untouched
Pro: Follows the exact pattern resources and prompts already use successfully
Con: Two schema fields on McpTool temporarily (zodSchema + inputSchema) unless we drop inputSchema
Con: Requires touching every tool file to add the Zod export
assumptions: The MCP SDK's server.tool() will continue to accept z.ZodRawShape
All current JSON Schema definitions can be cleanly expressed as Zod schemas
Some tool files already use Zod internally (idea.ts, shaping.ts) so those are trivial

data.name: Full Tool Descriptor with Zod as Source of Truth
data.description: Redefine the McpTool type so Zod IS the schema format. Each tool file exports a single descriptor: `{ name, description, schema: z.ZodRawShape, execute }`. Drop the JSON Schema inputSchema entirely. server.ts loops over tools and calls registerTool() with the descriptor fields. The tools/index.ts switch statement is also eliminated - each tool carries its own executor. The executeTool() function becomes a simple lookup by name from a Map built from the tools array. This is a deeper cleanup that removes both the dual registration AND the giant switch statement.
tradeoffs: Pro: Cleanest end state - one object per tool has everything needed
Pro: Eliminates the 35-case switch statement in tools/index.ts too
Pro: Adding a new tool = export one object from one file, add to array, done
Pro: No possibility of name/schema/executor getting out of sync
Con: Larger refactor - changes the McpTool type, every tool file, index.ts, and server.ts
Con: Needs to verify nothing external depends on the JSON Schema inputSchema format
Con: More risk of introducing bugs during the migration
assumptions: Nothing outside the MCP server consumes the JSON Schema inputSchema from McpTool
The execute function signatures are consistent enough to standardize
Tests can be updated to reflect the new structure

data.approach: Full Tool Descriptor with Zod as Source of Truth
data.reason: This is generated code that hasn't been fully reviewed yet. Going thorough now eliminates both the dual registration and the giant switch statement. Adding a new tool becomes: export one object, add to array, done. The switch statement is just another form of dual registration (name matched in two places). Clean it up properly once.
